title: I Took the Daycare Late-Pickup Fee to the Director's Own Pickup

parts.text: I ran in at 6:01 p.m. because the train stalled. The clock above the cubbies said 6:01. The director, Helen, charged me a late fee that started at 6:00 sharp. I was twenty-nine, parent, holding a toddler shoe. The handbook said fees begin at 6:05. I pointed at 6:05. Helen said the handbook was outdated. I photographed the handbook in the lobby binder, the clock, the receipt. Thursday I stayed to volunteer at the art table and watched Helen collect her grandson at 6:12 with no receipt. The same clock. The same binder.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: She billed me at 6:01 from an outdated page and collected her grandson at 6:12 for free.

social.video_title: The late fee started four minutes earlier for me — Part 1/2
social.description: Stalled train, toddler shoe, lobby binder vs. a grandson. Would you have argued at 6:01?

parts.text: I emailed the board of the nonprofit daycare with both times. They restored 6:05 and refunded me. Helen said volunteers should not spy. I was picking up my child, which is the opposite of spy. The clock stayed. The grandson still gets picked up, now before 6:05 like the rest of us. The shoe found its pair. The train still stalls. The fee waits five minutes, which is what the binder always wanted.

social.video_title: The board put 6:05 back on the clock — Part 2/2
social.description: Refund, one policy, no spy. Was a grandson a grace period?
